source.title: Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning: A View from Function Space
source.authors: A. Baratin; Thomas George; César Laurent; R. Devon Hjelm; Guillaume Lajoie; Pascal Vincent; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies network size and label corruption, then measures training and test error and compares generalization-gap trends with complexity measures. It does not use the specific interventions or measures in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 6 reports training and test error across hidden-layer sizes and label-corruption levels. Results cited from other studies were not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 6 directly measures training and test error while widening a one-hidden-layer MNIST MLP, training every network to cross-entropy 0.01. This bears on V2 using the original type of width intervention and error measures, although the supplied text does not preserve the plotted trend needed for a verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors observe task-dependent tangent-feature alignment and interpret it as feature selection and compression providing implicit regularization. Their proposed heuristic complexity measure correlates with generalization gaps across parameter counts and label corruption; practical neural-network benefits from SuperNat remain unestablished.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures tangent-feature dynamics and proposes a trajectory-based complexity measure; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that alignment effects vary with depth and learning rate; the generalization-gap comparison varies hidden-layer size and label-corruption proportion.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed trajectory-based complexity measure tracks the generalization-gap shape across parameter counts and label-corruption levels; the Figure 6 caption says a Neyshabur measure also does so.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A complexity measure combining SGD update norms and tangent-feature magnitudes tracks generalization gaps across network sizes and label-corruption levels.

fits_no_version.finding: For VGG19 on CIFAR-10 with high label noise, training-kernel effective rank decreases during improving test accuracy and rises when test accuracy deteriorates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training tangent-kernel effective rank can track learning and overfitting during training.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 measures changes in test-set output scores after perturbations along Jacobian singular vectors or random directions. It does not measure magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises or its association with generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network outputs are more sensitive to perturbations along leading Jacobian singular vectors than along most other tested directions.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2021
record.problems: The supplied text describes Figure 6’s generalization-gap trends but does not give numerical values for those plotted comparisons. No uncertainty estimates for these comparisons are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were retained. Figure 6 contains the relevant training and test error curves, but the supplied text does not give numerical values or state the specific trend needed to assign a result to V2. The other version-specific results are not reported as tests of those versions.

untested.parts: No fully randomized-label condition with readable held-out accuracy is reported. Partial label corruption does not establish the complete natural-label versus random-label comparison.

The supplied text does not establish the interpolation width or the direction of test-error changes beyond it. The activation function and absence of explicit regularization are also not specified for Figure 6.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of its generalization-gap rankings with norm and margin measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

record.verdict_notes: No result rows were supplied. Figure 6's relevant error curves are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Axis labels and the complexity-measure discussion alone cannot establish whether widening lowers test error after interpolation; no V2 verdict is justified from this text.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies the proportion of randomized labels, but does not report the specified comparison between fully random and natural labels for the same architecture and recipe.
The study varies hidden-layer size and displays training and test error, but the supplied text does not describe the test-error trend beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks’ test error is reported as a test of this version.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison is reported.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison is reported.
The study compares a trajectory-based tangent-feature complexity measure with other measures, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test its ranking of generalization gaps.
The study does not remove memorized training examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The width experiment directly bears on V2, although the extracted figure does not preserve the error trend needed to determine a verdict.

tranche.reason: Figure 6 varies hidden-layer width in a one-hidden-layer MNIST MLP and measures training and test error, matching V2's width intervention and error measures.
